codeReview.summary: Implementation covers all feature requirements: BIOS/ROM files and TempleOS ISO packaged via Emscripten file_packager.py with LZ4 compression, all artifacts organized in public/emulator/, Vite project configured with COOP/COEP headers on port 3200, reproducible packaging script created, 13 vitest tests added, and all artifacts committed (~56MB). The load.js correctly maps files to /pack/ paths and uses LZ4 compression. One potential runtime integration issue noted: the load.js expects Module['LZ4'] (from -sLZ4 compile flag) which may not be present in the QEMU JS glue — this is a cross-feature concern between the QEMU build and this packaging step that will surface at integration time. File ownership discrepancy (root-owned Docker outputs vs mojo-owned files) is cosmetic. Overall implementation is solid and well-structured.

issues.description: LZ4 runtime dependency: load.js asserts `typeof Module['LZ4'] === 'object'` for decompression, but qemu-system-x86_64.js has zero LZ4 references — the QEMU build may not have been compiled with -sLZ4. At runtime, data loading will fail unless the main module provides Module.LZ4. This is a cross-feature integration concern (QEMU build vs packaging) that should be verified during integration. If the QEMU build lacks -sLZ4, either rebuild QEMU with -sLZ4=1 or re-run file_packager without --lz4.

PACKAGE_NAME is '/out/qemu-system-x86_64.data' (Docker container path) used as internal identifier in addRunDependency/removeRunDependency and preloadResults. This is harmless since REMOTE_PACKAGE_BASE='qemu-system-x86_64.data' is used for actual fetching, but the Docker path leaking into the output is cosmetic noise.

File ownership: load.js and qemu-system-x86_64.data are owned by root (created inside Docker container), while .js and .wasm are owned by mojo. This won't affect serving but may cause permission issues during rebuilds or cleanup.

The trap cleanup uses unquoted $STAGING_DIR in 'rm -rf $STAGING_DIR'. While mktemp -d produces safe paths, best practice is to quote it: 'rm -rf "$STAGING_DIR"' to prevent issues with unexpected characters.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The LZ4 compression flag for file_packager (--lz4) requires the main Emscripten module to be compiled with -sLZ4=1 to provide the decompressor runtime. This dependency between file_packager flags and emcc flags is not documented anywhere in the project, and could cause integration failures.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: public/emulator/load.js contains: assert(typeof Module['LZ4'] === 'object', 'LZ4 not present - was your app build with -sLZ4?'). qemu-system-x86_64.js has 0 occurrences of 'LZ4'. Emscripten docs require -sLZ4 at compile time to enable Module.LZ4.

summary: Feature passes review. All required assets (4 BIOS/ROM files + TempleOS ISO) are correctly packaged via file_packager.py with LZ4 compression and /pack/ path mapping. Vite project is properly configured with COOP/COEP headers. 13 verification tests cover artifact existence, sizes, and load.js content correctness. The packaging script is reproducible. One cross-feature integration risk: LZ4 decompression at runtime requires Module.LZ4 from the QEMU JS glue (compiled with -sLZ4), which may not be present — this should be verified during frontend integration. Total committed size ~56MB as expected.
